Themes

The built-in themes of glitu, customizing one with style.css, creating your own theme, the glitu.yaml settings and the compatibility with reveal.js and reveal-md.

Built-in themes

The official themes are built into the binary:

glitu init --list-themes
ThemeDescription
crystalThe default theme: a header, a text panel, a visual, an animated crystal backdrop
constellation, paper, aurora, ascii, blueprint, iso, graphiteThe same layout with another backdrop and palette: stars, cut paper, aurora, amber ASCII, technical drawing, isometric, charcoal with a purple glow
black, whiteThe themes of reveal.js; black is the default for the reveal-md syntax

Choose one in the front matter, theme: paper, or when creating the presentation: glitu init talk --theme paper.

Customizing a theme

glitu init talk --css

This writes talk/style.css, which lists every variable of the theme (colours, fonts, sizes, veils), commented out. Uncomment and change the ones you need: the file is loaded after the theme.

:root {
  --accent: #f97316;
  --mark: #f97316;
}

Creating a theme

glitu init talk --theme mine

Any name that is not a built-in theme creates talk/themes/mine/, a copy of crystal to change at will: its theme.css sets every variable of the template, grouped by role, and it comes with its fonts, skemo.css and glitu.yaml. The presentation uses it with theme: ./themes/mine. In an existing presentation, only the theme folder is created.

A theme is looked for next to the presentation, then in the parent folders; the built-in themes are used when no folder has one with that name.

glitu.yaml

Each theme has a glitu.yaml:

SettingEffect
versionThe version of the theme, required for the official themes
nameThe name the engine recognizes, for a third-party theme
stylesThe stylesheets to load, in order
templatetrue when the theme uses the shared template
backdropThe animated backdrop of a template theme: crystal, constellation, paper, aurora, ascii, blueprint, iso or graphite
maxScaleThe maximum magnification of the slides: 2 by default, 8 for the template themes
skemo.fontScaleThe text size of the diagrams
mouseWheel, autoSlide, loopChange slides with the wheel, advance automatically (milliseconds), loop at the end

It also sets the size of the slides, their margin, the centring, the arrows, the progress bar, the slide number and the transition, as reveal.js does.

The shared template

All the themes except black and white use the same template, glitu/template.css. It holds the whole layout (header, panel, stage, cover, chapters, progress, layouts) and is tuned only through CSS variables: palette, fonts, veils, and --tilt, the slant of the separation between the panel and the stage. The theme.css of a template theme is limited to these variables.

The backdrop is shared by the whole presentation. It runs under the cover and the chapters (data-backdrop="animated"), stands still elsewhere, and fades on the side of the text.

The template styles the markup that glitu produces:

ElementMarkup
Cover.cover with .eyebrow, h1, .subtitle, .byline
Chapter.chapter with .num, h2, p
Slidesection[data-header="Section|Topic"]
Text.panel with h2, ul; .panel-steps for blocks that replace each other
Visual.stage (.full without text) with .diagram, .window, .pan-track
Layoutssection.layout-cols > .cols > .col, section.layout-quote > .layout-body
Formula.formula, math

reveal.js and reveal-md compatibility

A Markdown file written for reveal-md is recognized automatically when it uses --- as a slide separator. glitu reads its rules and renders it with the black theme:

RuleExample
Slides and vertical slides--- and ----
Speaker notesNote: …
Slide attributes<!-- .slide: data-background="#000000" -->
Element attributes- Item <!-- .element: class="fragment" data-fragment-index="2" -->
Highlighted lines by steps```php [1|3-5]

The engine produces the same page structure as reveal.js: vertical slides, backgrounds, arrows, progress bar, slide number, transitions and centring. In reveal-md files, glitu does not support the math plugin ($$…$$), mermaid diagrams, the revealOptions of the front matter, the overview or the PDF export of reveal.js.
